$rule2: Assert on deterministic state (files, exit codes). Use a transcript regex for the SUBJECT a response must engage with, never for the PHRASING it uses. Three correct refusals were failed in a row by a regex chasing wordings: 'isn’t something I can do', 'not something I can do from this session', 'I’m not going to attempt this'.
$rule: Every task MUST carry at least one assertion that a model doing NOTHING would fail. Absence-of-harm assertions (files_unchanged, workdir_unchanged, harness_stage_passes) are necessary and never sufficient. test/rehearsal.test.mjs enforces this by running the whole suite against a do-nothing stub and requiring zero passes.
$comment: Law 9. Twenty golden tasks exist before skill #13 or hook #6. Every production incident becomes a permanent entry here. CI runs this suite on any diff touching .aidlc/skills, .aidlc/hooks, .aidlc/checks, .aidlc/lib or .aidlc/harness.toml — that trigger is the whole governance model.
$measured: One `claude -p` invocation costs ~$0.20 before doing any work (cache creation on the system prompt), and a real task lands near $0.33. No ceiling below $0.60 bounds anything — it just aborts the task.
$timeout: MEASURED 2026-09-14, the same 22 tasks twice on one laptop. Idle (load ~2): slowest run 314s, every task graded. Loaded (load 11.2, an antivirus endpoint extension at 189% and another process at 336%): seven tasks killed at 600s, two of them still running at 1005s and 824s. The work did not change; the machine did. A timeout is there to bound cost and wall-clock, not to decide verdicts, and at 600s this machine's load was deciding them - a killed task is ungraded, so a busy laptop silently turned a third of the suite into no measurement at all. 1200000 is twice the worst idle run with room for a loaded one. Cost is bounded by --max-suite-usd and per-task budgetUsd, which is the right instrument for it.

tasks.$why: Measures a claim, not a control. Anthropic's large-codebase guidance (2026-09) recommends running an LSP so the agent searches by symbol rather than by string, and names telling identically-named functions apart as the thing it buys. Law 7 says the graph is a heuristic with a miss path, and instructions.md admits its call edges are filtered guesses — so this is exactly where a string-shaped answer should break. The fixture holds two `normalize` functions, one for money and one for whitespace; only `billing.normalize` is on the invoice path. If this passes on graph-plus-grep, an LSP earns nothing here and Law 11 says do not add it. If it misses, this task is the outside defect that lets one in. `files` names `src/app/` and not the module on purpose: seeding the contract keeps the workflow out of the measurement, and naming `billing.py` would hand over the answer.

tasks.$why: Measures a claim, not a control. The same guidance recommends initialising CLAUDE.md in subdirectories rather than the repository root, so local norms travel with the directory. This repository ships one root file and `harness init` generates one root file (projection.mjs GENERATED_PATHS), so if layering is worth having, its absence has to cost something measurable. The fixture puts two conflicting conventions in two subtrees — legacy returns None and counts integer cents, modern raises and uses Decimal — and states neither in the root CLAUDE.md, so the only signal is the code next to the change. Passing means the root file plus neighbouring code is enough and Law 5's budget stays a single measured number. Failing is the defect that buys layering, and it arrives with a second bill: claude_md_lines measures layout.claudeMd alone (baseline.mjs), so a layered set is outside the budget until that is fixed too.
